summary.headline: CPCL posted record FY26 crude throughput of 11.71 MMT (112% of capacity) and Q4 GRM of $13.75/bbl versus Singapore's $8.70.
summary.overview: Management reported record operational performance for Q4 and FY26, with crude throughput of 2.93 MMT in Q4 (111% of installed capacity) and 11.71 MMT for the year, despite a one-month shutdown of one of three crude units. FY26 GRM was $9.2/bbl versus Singapore's $5.83/bbl, and Q4 GRM was $13.75/bbl, though management cited a core GRM of $10.3/bbl for Q4. Forex losses of about INR200 crore in Q4 and about INR350-400 crore for the year were booked in other expenses, and gross borrowings fell to about INR1,900 crore with net borrowings of INR973 crore. Management raised the FY26 dividend to INR62 per share (including an INR8 interim) and outlined about INR2,000 crore of growth capex over 2-3 years plus about INR500 crore a year of maintenance capex.

segments.name: Refining
segments.commentary: Crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY26 and 2.93 MMT in Q4, both records, with diesel (HSD) output of 5.139 MMT and petrol (MS) of 1.318 MMT, both highest ever. Distillate yield reached 79.1%, and DCU utilisation rose from about 70% to close to 100%.

segments.name: Niche / value-added products
segments.commentary: Niche products (about 7-8% of volume, including LS naphtha, pharma-grade hexane, MTO) contribute about 15% of margins per management. Hexane capacity doubled from 30 to 60 (units not specified); MTO volumes more than doubled in FY26. Trial runs started on pentane and textile-grade MTO.

segments.name: Marketing / retail
segments.commentary: About 90-92% of product is sold to Indian Oil under a long-term agreement at refinery transfer price (RTP). Around 300 retail outlet licences were obtained, with commissioning expected in FY27; the retail project is about INR400 crore.

guidance_outlook: No planned major M&I in the first six months of FY27; a scheduled M&I of one crude/refinery unit is expected around September-October 2026, which will affect throughput.
Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project (250 KTPA capacity, INR1,600 crore) has all approvals and execution is under way; IRR-based and aimed at higher realisations.
About INR2,000 crore (LOBS INR1,600 crore plus retail INR400 crore) to be spent over 2-3 years, plus about INR500 crore per year normal capex.
Low-cost debottlenecking and secondary capacity study with EIL expected to complete in FY27; capex not yet frozen and not in current plan.
Management expects momentum to continue into FY27; net debt ratio stated as comfortable and capacity to borrow for projects is available.
Bonus issue to be considered by the Board at the appropriate time.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR856 crore versus INR673 crore in FY25.
Group 2/3 LOBS unit of 250 KTPA (INR1,600 crore); execution started, approvals in place.
Retail outlet programme of about 300 outlets (INR400 crore), with bulk of commissioning in FY27.
Installed crude capacity referenced at 10.5 MMT; company has consistently run above this for 3-4 years, reaching 11.6-11.7 MMT.
Crude sourcing: 52% high sulphur and 48% low sulphur in FY26; 55-60% under 1-year term contracts (almost all Middle East), remainder spot. Refinery can process up to 70% high-sulphur crude.
demand_pricing: Q4 GRM US$13.75/bbl reported and US$10.3/bbl core, against Singapore US$8.70/bbl; management said net GRM on realised RTP was close to long-term average (about US$13/bbl for diesel and ATF) over the most recent month.
Export duties on diesel and ATF were imposed from 26 March 2026; management said export is optional, and it is not booking exports under compulsion.

Crude mix in FY26 (approximate): India about 10%, Russia 25-30%, Middle East the majority (including Iraq), Africa and US 5-10%. Around 30-40% of Middle East term volumes were disrupted briefly, with suppliers assuring make-up cargoes.
Inventory: crude about 5-18 days (around 20 days normal); product inventory only a few days, dispatched to IOCL.
Management said LPG maximisation (447 TMT vs 404 TMT) did not hurt margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will throughput stay at 110-111% in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects no M&I in the first six months; utilisation above 100% attributed to good upkeep and fewer unplanned interruptions. A scheduled M&I is expected around September-October 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core versus reported Q4 GRM, and what was the forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Core GRM is US$10.3/bbl versus reported US$13.75/bbl. Forex loss was about INR200 crore in Q4 and about INR350 crore for FY26, per the call (later cited as INR400 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Is net GRM after export duty and RTP adjustment still healthy for diesel and ATF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net GRM on realised RTP is close to long-term averages, around US$13/bbl, and that the monthly view is what counts. It declined to comment on media reports of OMC discount demands.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics and capex of the LOBS project and low-cost debottlenecking?
qa_highlights.answer: LOBS is IRR-based, shifting volumes from Group 1 to Group 2/3 lube feedstock. Debottlenecking is at study stage with EIL, expected to complete in FY27, with capex not in current plan.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to forex losses booked in other expenses: INR634 crore in Q4 and INR2,001 crore for FY26. A separate note was not provided due to disclosure classification norms.

risks_watch: Crude supply disruption: Strait of Hormuz closure for over 50 days and 30-40% short-term disruption to Middle East term volumes; make-up cargoes assured but not yet confirmed.
Export duty and RTP mechanics on diesel and ATF; management declined to confirm any OMC discount arrangement.
Forex losses (INR350-400 crore in FY26) flowing through other expenses; watch for further INR-denominated impact.
Scheduled M&I around September-October 2026 could pull down throughput from above-100% levels.
Execution of INR2,000 crore growth capex (LOBS and retail) and commissioning of about 300 outlets in FY27.
Management did not quantify profit foregone from RTP-based sales to IOCL when asked.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and dividends, but guarded on near-term market questions: management repeatedly declined to give daily cracks, crude prices, OMC pricing or export-duty impact, steering answers to monthly averages and long-term norms.
key_quotes: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.
I found around 13 $/bbl to be the long-term average.
My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.
I'm not a trader. My objective is not to take advantage or get bogged down by short-term few days abnormal situation.
